title: Applied ML: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Guardrails, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes and operational checklists for: the eval harness, creation and maintenance of prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile development, and regression triage. It is intended for Applied ML, Model Onboarding, and SRE partners who ship model updates to production serving.

Goals

- Ensure consistent, reproducible evaluation across model variants and infra targets.
- Catch quality regressions early via automated evaluations and alerting.
- Provide deterministic procedures for quantization profiling and safety/quality guardrails.
- Define a clear triage and rollout path for any regressions that impact production SLA or customer quality.

Scope

Applies to all model types onboarded to Redwood serving (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, instruction-tuned chat models, rerankers, and embedding models). Not in scope: experimental research-only checkpoints not intended for serving.

Key Roles and Ownership

- Applied ML (owner): maintains eval harness, prompt set catalog, and automated pipelines.
- Model Onboarding (owner): runs onboarding checklist, labeling, and production readiness signoff.
- Eng SRE (stakeholder): ensures infra SLOs, provides perf / latency baselines and rollout guards.
- Customer Success (stakeholder): verifies customer-facing benchmarks for enterprise customers as needed.

Standards and SLOs

- Eval coverage: every model must have at least 3 representative prompt sets (small/dev, medium/qa, large/production) before canary.
- Quality SLOs (examples):
  - Instruction-following models: instruction-exact-match >= 88% or relative delta <= 1.5% vs baseline on production prompt set.
  - Summarization: ROUGE-L >= baseline -2.0 points and fluency score >= 4.0 (1-5 Likert).
  - Embeddings: cosine similarity on benchmark pairs >= baseline -0.03.
  - Latency SLO: p95 decode latency <= 400ms for short text (<=128 tokens) on Dedicated tier (measured on canary infra).
  - Token-reliability: token error rate (exceptions/timeouts) <= 0.2% per 24h.

Eval Harness: Standards and Pipeline

1) Harness requirements
   - Tests run in CI and nightly pipelines; outputs are deterministic artifacts (JSON + CSV + HTML report).
   - All tests must pin model hash, tokenizer version, quantization profile, and inference config (batch size, max tokens, temperature).
   - Outputs must include: per-example outputs, metric breakdowns, delta vs baseline, and representative failure examples.

2) Execution environments
   - Local reproducibility: docker image redwood/eval-harness:{semver} with pinned python deps.
   - CI: GitHub Actions workflow eval-harness.yml triggers on PRs to model-onboarding and on merges to release branches. Nightly runs on a Dedicated small GPU job.

3) Required artifact fields (example JSON keys; harness will validate presence):
   - model_id, model_hash, tokenizer_version, quant_profile, eval_set_id, run_id, commit_sha, metrics_summary_url

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

- Catalog organization: /prompt-sets/{domain}/{use-case}/{size}-{version}. Each entry in the catalog must contain: description, target-distribution (tokens, qps), labeling instructions, expected metric(s) and baseline values, and owner.
- Prompt set tiers:
  - dev (<=200 examples): fast feedback during PRs.
  - qa (500-2k examples): used for release candidate gating.
  - production (5k+ examples): used for continuous monitoring and SLA verification.

- Benchmarks must include negative controls, adversarial perturbations, and edge-case distribution slices (e.g., long-context, numeric reasoning, multilingual).

Model Onboarding Checklist (must be completed before canary)

1) Basic metadata and artifacts
   - Provide model card: architecture, pretraining data summary, tokenizer, supported sequence length, licenses.
   - Upload model artifact to model registry with immutable model_hash.

2) Eval and guardrail pass
   - Run eval harness against dev, qa, and production prompt sets.
   - Quality metrics must meet thresholds in this playbook or have documented product exception.

3) Performance and infra validation
   - Perf profile: p50/p95 decode latencies, GPU memory footprint, KV cache size at typical sequence lengths.
   - Autoscaling smoke test: simulated QPS to verify Dedicated capacity policies.

4) Security and compliance checks
   - Scans for PII leakage on representative corpora (automated PII detector run).
   - Confirm allowed licenses and data provenance.

5) Rollout plan and rollback criteria
   - Canary size: default 5% traffic for 24 hours with automatic rollback if: error rate delta > 0.5% absolute OR quality metric delta (primary metric) > 2.0% relative.

Quality Guardrails

- Types of guardrails
  - Safety (toxicity, policy compliance).
  - Reliability (timeouts, malformed outputs).
  - Correctness (factually incorrect claims for knowledge-grounded tasks).
  - Distributional drift detection (embedding-based drift monitors).

- Implementation patterns
  - Pre-response filters: plugin-level checks (prompt sanitization, length caps).
  - Post-response validators: classifier-based safety checks, regex/structural validators for structured outputs.
  - Automated fallback: when guardrail fails, route to lower-capacity but higher-precision model variant or return safe default per route policy.

- Example thresholds (configurable per customer/route):
  - Toxicity score threshold (Perspective-like): >= 0.85 -> block; 0.6-0.85 -> warn/flag.
  - Hallucination detector confidence >= 0.7 -> flag for human review for RAG workflows.

Quantization Profiles and Profiling Playbook

- Purpose: reduce memory and cost while preserving quality. Quantization profiles are first-class artifacts and must be versioned and pinned for each serving variant.

- Recommended quantization pipeline
  1) Baseline: evaluate FP16/FP32 metrics to get target baseline.
  2) Static activation profiling: collect activation ranges on representative prompts (use profile-runner --profile-activations).
  3) Candidate quant steps: 8-bit PTQ (symmetric/asymmetric), 4-bit quant-aware fine-tuning (QAT) experiments.
  4) Evaluate candidates: run full eval harness on qa + production prompt sets and compare metric deltas.
  5) Perf validation: measure latency, memory, and p95 tail changes on canary infra.
  6) Signoff: quant_profile artifact (json) with fields: profile_id, technique, sample_size, baseline_metrics, delta_metrics, infra_target.

- Example CLI snippets
  - Profile activations: docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data redwood/quant-tools:prod profile --model /models/mymodel --prompts /prompt-sets/prod.json --out /data/profiles/mymodel-20260601.json
  - Evaluate quant candidate: python eval_harness/run.py --model /models/mymodel_q8 --eval-set /prompt-sets/qa.json --out /reports/mymodel_q8_report.json

Regression Triage Playbook

1) Alerting and first-response
   - Automated alerts: generated when nightly or canary runs report primary metric regression beyond configured thresholds (example: instruction-exact-match relative delta > 1.5% or latency p95 increase > 20%). Alerts post to #applied-ml-regression and create a ticket in JIRA under PM-REG.
   - Pager rotation: on-call Applied ML engineer (primary) must acknowledge within 30 minutes.

2) Initial validation (within 2 hours)
   - Re-run failing eval with pinned artifacts (model hash, tokenizer, quant_profile) to rule out transient infra or data pipeline errors.
   - Check drift signals: embedding-distance from baseline, recent training data changes, tokenization diffs.

3) Root cause classification
   - Categories: model-code change, tokenizer change, quantization delta, data/regressor drift, infra/perf degradation, test/metric bug.

4) Mitigation and rollback
   - If root cause is model-related and regression is above rollout thresholds, trigger immediate rollback to previous model hash and run a smoke canary.
   - If root cause is quantization or infra, promote fallback variant (e.g., FP16 variant) and schedule a hotfix.

5) Postmortem and continuous improvement
   - Postmortem within 7 business days: owner documents timeline, RCA, mitigation, and corrective actions.
   - Update prompt sets, add failing examples to regression suite, and schedule additional guardrail rules if needed.

Operational Playbook Checklist (quick steps)

- Before canary: run eval-harness full-suite, perf smoke tests, signoff in model registry.
- During canary (0-24h): monitor primary metrics, p95 latency, and error rate; check for safety flags; be prepared to rollback.
- After successful canary: promote model and add nightly monitoring job for first 7 days with stricter alert thresholds.

Appendices

A. Example minimal model-card snippet (YAML)

model_id: mymodel-v1
architecture: decoder-only
max_sequence: 4096
tokenizer: sentencepiece-128k
license: apache-2.0
quant_profile: q8-symmetric-v1
owner: applied-ml

B. Example run command for CI (GitHub Actions)

# .github/workflows/eval-harness.yml snippet
jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run eval harness
        run: |
          docker build -t redwood/eval-harness:${{ github.sha }} -f docker/eval-harness.Dockerfile .
          docker run --rm -e MODEL=/models/${{ matrix.model }} -v ${{ github.workspace }}:/workspace redwood/eval-harness:${{ github.sha }} \n            python run.py --model $MODEL --eval-set /workspace/prompt-sets/dev.json --out /workspace/reports/${{ matrix.model }}.json

C. Governance: when to request a product exception

- A product exception is required when a model does not meet a standard threshold but is requested for special-cased customer reasons (e.g., proprietary domain performance). The exception must be documented with: risk assessment, mitigation plan, and a sunset date.
